experiment: E64 readout64: a Jain et al. 2024 Def 1 linear readout per block of the 67M target model over the pair's 64 table values (E54's 32 elicit and 32 cipher values), trained on Pile positions and never on the tables, read on E54's held-out windows against W0's own possessed set; and a causal check that removes the target value's readout row from the residual in the twelve saved E54/E56 fine-tunes
plan: reports/plans/2026-11-02_plan_baseline-next3-draft.md, option 1 (approved by the user 2026-11-02, ask #9), its 'Amendment before filing (2026-11-02)' and the writer's note under it. Earlier drafts called it E62

amended_2026-11-02: After the code review (reports/reviews/2026-11-02_review_e64-code.md, F1-F8, all accepted by the lead) and before any reading: nothing has run on E64, on a GPU or otherwise on the model or a saved state, so F1 and every other change apply before any reading and no rule here was chosen knowing an outcome. The first-filed value of every changed entry is under superseded_2026-11-02. Plan: section 'After the code review (2026-11-02)'
code: experiments/readout64/run.py; src/commute/readout.py section E64 (E59's functions above it unchanged); tests/test_readout64.py; cluster/readout64.sbatch
claim: Some block before the last holds the elicit values, key-specifically, as a linear readout trained on the Pile over the 64 values, and not the cipher's; removing that direction costs the elicit fine-tunes more of their gain than the ciphers.
null: The elicit values are held only where the readout is the output (last block), or the removal costs both kinds the same share: the label is the construction and r reads the prior.

settings.model: the 67M target model (steering.Net), fp32, TF32 off; means in float64
settings.sites_note: block b (0-3): its readout reads block b's output residual, the next block's input (site in<b+1>), and for the last block its output before the final RMSNorm (out3). 'Before the last block' = blocks 0, 1, 2. As E59
settings.values: the 64 values: stage1.json's 32 elicit and 32 cipher values, checked unique (readout.pair_values; jq on stage1.json before filing: 64 distinct); both tasks share their 32 keys
settings.readout: probe.Probes with 64 outputs: per block d=768 -> 64, nn.Linear init, bias kept; a 64-way next-token loss
settings.schedule_source: Jain et al. 2024 L1238-1248 as copied in src/commute/probe.py, as E59; batch 96 and AdamW's library defaults filled in there (E55). A batch here is 96 positions, not 96 windows
settings.training_data: a position is a window of 41 tokens of a Pile row with the next token at index 21, so the residual is read at index 20, the answer position of E54's task windows (same context length, same distance from the attention sink at index 0). Fit rows: Pile train rows 32768-61439, held rows 61440-65535 (never the task rows 0-32767). At most `cap` windows per value (`held_cap` on the held rows) drawn by a seeded permutation. Batches are drawn uniformly with replacement from the pooled windows
settings.row_quality_readout: F2: a second readout, same schedule and seed, on the first 241 of each value's drawn windows (readout.capped_idx: a random draw and a subset of the scored readout's windows; a value under 241 keeps what it has, so the rare elicit values stay thin). No early bars, since it only reads P2's row quality; a non-finite loss still stops. Weights at results/large/readouts_low_cap.pt. 241 is the cipher's minimum windows per value in measured_before_filing; stage 0 stops if the run counts another
settings.rank: rank of a window's target value among the 64 at the answer position = 1 + the number of the 64 scored strictly higher (ties share a rank); a key's rank = the lower median over its windows
settings.specific: for key k with value v: L = lower median of log P(v) over k's windows minus lower median of log P(v) over the other keys' windows (P = softmax over the 64); specific iff L >= log 3 (inclusive). Read in logs, so no denominator can vanish. Plan's '3 times its median over the other 31 keys' windows'
settings.possessed_keys: for logits on a pool of windows: keys with median rank <= 5 and specific; an unfit value's key is out for a readout, and counts for W0 (W0 is not trained)
settings.M: W0's own possessed set: the possessed_keys rule on W0's logits restricted to the 64 values. Computed per task and per pool: M (all 97 held-out windows) and M_fit (fit half, even indices, 28 of 32 keys covered)
settings.elicit_possession: block b possesses the elicit map on a pool iff |possessed keys at b, intersected with the pool's M| / |pool's M| >= 3/4 (inclusive). Keys outside M do not count (reported as outside_ref). Empty M: not possessed
settings.cipher_possession: block b possesses the cipher iff its number of possessed cipher keys >= 6, inclusive, on any pool and whatever |M| is: 3/4 of min_M, readout.cipher_possession(own, min_M, 3, 4). The bar is fixed so that it is a statement about the cipher: a bar growing with |elicit M| read 11 of 32 cipher keys as 'not possessed' at |M| = 16, and the cipher's own M, expected empty, cannot be a denominator. The elicit bar stays 3/4 of |M|. Chance is 2.5 keys
settings.l_star: the earliest block before the last at which the elicit map is possessed on the fit half (against M_fit); None if none, or if |M_fit| < 6 (3/4 of min_M; inclusive at 6; readout.l_star64). P2 voids with the reason
settings.removal: at block l* only and at the answer position only, the residual has its component along a unit vector removed: h <- h - (h.u) u; u = block l*'s readout row for the window's target value, normalised (rows are indexed by the 64 values). Applied to the state's own forward. Softmax ignores a component shared by every row, so each row's cosine with the mean row is reported (expected small). Readout.ablation unchanged from E59: this code has never run on a GPU (E59 stopped before it)
settings.A: readout.shares' A_lo, E59's amended rule: (the state's mean log-odds drop under the removal minus W0's, same windows and direction) / the state's log-odds gain G_logodds, scoring half (odd indices, 48 windows); nan if |G_logodds| < floor_min; a negative gain gives a well-defined share, scored as is
settings.random_direction: the do-nothing: one Gaussian unit vector per distinct target value (readout.random_dirs), same removal at the same block; A_rand defined as A
settings.states: the twelve saved weight changes: experiments/keydependent_elicit/results/large/{elicit,cipher,cipher_own}_s{0,1}.pt (sha256 in stage2.json finetunes) and experiments/keydependent_patch/results/large/{elicit,cipher}_s{2,3,4}.pt (sha256 in job2.json finetunes), links into ~/commute-data/results-large. On disk and sha256-matched to their records 2026-11-02 by the writer. cipher_own_s2-s4 were never saved (job2.json sha256 null), so the own-step clause reads s0, s1

early_checks.note: readout.early_miss64: over the last 50 batches, x = last block's loss (max) or its loss minus the model's on the same batch (max_over_model); stops iff mean(x) - 3 * sd(x) / sqrt(50) is not <= the bar, so the bar is read off a batch sd measured in the run, not one batch (E59's job 48344 stopped on batch noise). Step 250: the bar is the entropy of the sample's values, computed in the run (readout.early_checks64, about 3.8 from the filed counts), minus 0.2, so a readout that learned only the value frequencies stops: its batch sd is about 0.08, so the 3 standard errors are about 0.03. ln 64 was the wrong chance level, because the sample is not balanced. Step 2000: 0.5 is E59's first-filed margin at this step; relative to the model because E59's absolute bar misfired. The capped readout has no bars

threshold_sources.frac 3/4, min_M 8, max_cipher_M 2: the lead's amendment, from job 48453: on the 97 windows W0's own ranks read 16 of 32 elicit keys in E59's band where the rule needed 24
threshold_sources.the 6 keys of cipher_possession and l*: the review's F1 and F4, the lead's decision: 3/4 of min_M, the filing's own 'at least 6 keys'
threshold_sources.row_quality_cap 241, below_entropy 0.2: the review's F2 and F7, the lead's decision; 241 measured on the fit rows, 0.2 ours
threshold_sources.max_unfit 8: the plan's edge case for elicit; applied to the cipher as well by the lead's 'if too many values are unfit, stage 0 stops'
threshold_sources.cap, held_cap, fit_row_count: cap from the plan; the held rows are one eighth of the rows, and held_cap is one eighth of cap, so the held-out sample has the training sample's prior. Val rows are too few: the cached val_0_256 holds under 50 positions for 18 elicit and 32 cipher values

measured_before_filing.positions: numpy on the cached rows, no model. Windows per value on the fit rows: elicit min 26, median 3207, cipher min 241, median 346. Under 200: two elicit values, 13905 (147 windows, key 1495) and 42344 (26, key 3907), no cipher value. Under the cap of 2000: 13 elicit, all 32 cipher. About 57,000 fit windows, so 4000 batches of 96 pass over each about 7 times. Stage 0 prints these counts; a change from them means the rows changed
measured_before_filing.states: 12 of 12 sha256 equal their records (E54 stage2.json, E56 job2.json)
measured_before_filing.model_at_full_vocabulary: job 48453, m1_check.json: elicit 16 keys in rank band 2-20 and 17 at rank <= 20 of 50,277; cipher all 32 above rank 100. Not yet read at 64 ways; M is unknown until stage 0

stage0.order: first and alone, cheapest first; run.json is written after each step; every miss exits 1 before any removal on a fine-tuned state is scored
checks: inputs: windows_{elicit,cipher}.pt sha256 equal stage1.json's; keys and values equal stage1.json's; W0's geometric-mean P(target) |rate / stage1 rate - 1| <= rate_rel_tol; each of the twelve states' sha256 equals its record and its gain G equals the filed G within reproduce_tol. Stop on a miss
model: elicit |M| >= 8 (else stop: the pair cannot carry the reading at this rule, the user decides); cipher |M| <= 2 (else stop: the construction check cannot pass)

positions: per value on the fit rows, a value under 200 unfit (which, printed); stop if over 8 values are unfit in either task, or if M's fit keys are under 3/4 of M; stop if the cipher's minimum is not row_quality_cap

readouts: early checks (thresholds.early_checks) on the scored readout, or a non-finite loss on either readout, stop the job; weights saved at once to results/large/readouts.pt and readouts_low_cap.pt with sha256
fit: see stage0.fit. Recorded, not a stop
P3, the construction check: stop on a miss
do-nothing: every state's |A_rand| <= 0.05 at the removal block. Stop on a miss

W0 positive control, when l* exists: over the scoring-half windows of M's keys, the lower median of W0's log P(target) drop under the target value's row >= 0.3 nats, and strictly above the same median under a wrong value's row (next index in the same task, wrapping; same windows). The random direction is read on the same windows, reported. Stop on a miss, P2 void
stage0.tolerance_sources: E56's filed tolerance; E59's stage 0 measured dG = 0 in all four logs
stage0.fit: the scored last block's 64-way held-out loss <= W0's own 64-way restricted loss on the same windows, moved to the sample's prior (F3: a value over the cap loses log(count / cap), the shift W0_training_prior uses), + 0.1. One-sided. W0 at its natural prior is logged beside it, not read: its loss on a capped sample is inflated by the values over the cap, a margin the readout would get free. Recorded, not a stop: the plan's edge case (a pass stands; an elicit-clause or P2 miss reads 'unreadable'; hard cap one training run) overrides the general line in its 'Control first' paragraph, as E59's last amendment did; P3 reads the same readouts and does stop. See the plan's writer's note

P1.statement: The elicit map is possessed at block 0, 1 or 2 (relative to M), and the cipher at no block (all 97 windows)
P1.rule: readout.p1 on the flags of elicit_possession and cipher_possession: pass iff some block < 3 possesses the elicit map and no block 0-3 possesses the cipher
P1.threshold: at least 3/4 of M's keys, inclusive; for the cipher at least 6 keys, a fixed bar (3/4 of min_M), inclusive; each key median rank <= 5 of 64 and specific
P1.absolute_or_relative: relative to the model's own possessed set; the rank and specificity bars are the same on the model and the readout
P1.blind_to: non-linear encodings; a direction the model does not read; keys W0 itself does not pass (outside M, reported as outside_ref, a bigram-like early block can hold them); the training sample's prior (capped: the cipher's rows see about 350 windows, the common elicit values' 2000, a tilt of up to about 1.7 nats against the cipher in rank, which the specificity guard does not see)
P1.noise_floor: about 3 windows per key, one readout seed. Chance: rank <= 5 of 64 gives 2.5 of 32 keys before the specificity guard, against the elicit bar of at least 6 keys and the cipher bar of 6

P2.statement: A separates the five elicit states from the five matched ciphers at l* by E51's rule; the cipher at its own step reads within 0.1 of its matched A
P2.rule: readout.p2 on A_lo, unchanged: elicit.separation(elicit s0-s4, cipher s0-s4, min_gap 0.2) verdict a_higher, and |A(cipher_own_s) - A(cipher_s)| < 0.1 (strict) on s0, s1
P2.threshold: gap > larger within-kind range and gap >= 0.2; own-step difference < 0.1
P2.absolute_or_relative: relative (a share of each state's own log-odds gain, net of W0's drop)
P2.blind_to: a route that re-encodes the value off the readout direction; directions other than the one row; keys outside M enter A (A is over all scoring-half windows, as E59's rule, and the gain is over all keys). the sample size behind each row: cipher rows see about 350 windows and common elicit rows 2000, a worse-fitted row is a noisier direction whose removal costs less, and that alone pushes A towards elicit above cipher, P2's pass direction. The capped readout tests this; its rows are over-fitted for both arms (about 15,000 windows, about 49,000 parameters per block), and the rare elicit values stay under the cap (26 and 147 windows at least)
P2.control: W0's drop over M's windows, at the bar and above a wrong value's row; the do-nothing; the last-block removal on every state, reported, expected near 1 (A can read high); the capped readout's A at l* for both arms, for the row-quality reading
P2.noise_floor: A_rand per state, bound 0.05; the within-kind range over five seeds enters the rule
P2.row_quality_reading: Filed before any run (F2). P2's verdict is computed as in `rule`, on the scored readout. The same separation rule (elicit.separation, min_gap 0.2) runs on A from the capped readout at the same block, s0-s4 of both arms. A P2 pass where that does not read a_higher (none, b_higher, or unreadable from a nan) reads 'not separable from row quality', and the branch says so rather than 'the pair's label is causal'. The own-step clause is not in this reading; its numbers are reported. A P2 fail, void or unreadable keeps its reading whatever the capped readout reads: reported only
P2.void_when: l* None, for no block possessing on the fit half or |M_fit| under 6 (the removal runs at the last block, reported, not scored; the reason is in P2), or W0's positive control fails (the run stops)

P3.statement: The construction check, relative to the model: the last-block readout possesses at least 3/4 of M, the cipher's M has at most 2 keys, and the last-block readout does not possess the cipher
P3.threshold: 3/4 inclusive; at most 2 inclusive; cipher_possession: at least 6 last-block cipher keys is possessed, a miss
P3.absolute_or_relative: relative. Replaces the plan's >= 24 elicit keys and >= 24 cipher keys at rank > 20 of 64, both absolute: the first by the lead's amendment, the second given the same treatment here (W0's and the last block's counts at rank > 20 are printed, not scored)
P3.lean: the plan: high. The writer's: medium, because M is read with W0's natural prior over the values and the readout is trained at a capped one, so a common value's rank can differ for that reason alone. W0_training_prior is reported to read a miss
P3.noise_floor: the fit (stage0.fit); about 3 windows per key

expected_table.before training: W0: elicit |M| likely 8-24 (16-17 keys pass at full vocabulary, and some fall to the specificity guard); cipher |M| 0-2. Do-nothing and control: none yet
expected_table.early training: step 0 loss near ln 64 = 4.16 per block (a default-init linear map); step 250 last-block mean under the entropy of the sample's values minus 0.2 (about 3.6), which is not measured: E59's last block had covered 81% of its whole fall by step 250 at this learning rate (jobs 48279, 48357), which here reads under the bar if the final loss is under about 3.5; step 2000 within 0.5 of the model
expected_table.fit: last block's held-out loss at or below W0's restricted loss at the sample's prior + 0.1; held-in lower than held-out (about 49,000 parameters per block on about 57,000 positions: over-fitting is possible and the gap is reported). Capped readout, reported: held-out loss above the scored readout's, held-in further below it (about 15,000 positions)
expected_table.possession: last block: >= 3/4 of M; block 0: may hold keys outside M; if claim, elicit at some block <= 2 and cipher at none; if null, elicit at the last only
expected_table.W0 control: median drop >= 0.3 nats over M's windows at l*, above the wrong row's on the same windows; the cipher's and the random direction's drops reported, random near 0
expected_table.A: if claim: elicit above matched cipher by the rule, own-step cipher within 0.1. If null: no separation. Last block: near 1 on every state, reported
expected_table.W0_training_prior: reported, never scored: W0's possessed set after moving a value over the cap down by log(count / cap). Expected nearer the last-block readout's set than M is

decision_tree.P1 pass, P2 pass: with P2's separation also a_higher on the capped readout: the pair's label is causal and VPD-independent; write up; the Qwen KV table carries it
decision_tree.P2 pass, capped readout does not read a_: not separable from row quality: the label is not shown causal, whatever P1 reads; report and tell the user
decision_tree.P1 elicit at the last block only, P2 voi: 'half-known' means what the output says; r's separation of this pair is a reading of the prior, written so
decision_tree.P2 fail: r's reading of this pair has no causal footing; the line pauses on the 67M and E55 C2 decides r's standing, whatever the capped readout reads (reported)
decision_tree.P2 pass, P1 fail: not in the plan's tree (a cipher possessed, or l* on the fit half alone): report and tell the user
decision_tree.fit missed: a pass stands; an elicit-clause or P2 miss reads unreadable
decision_tree.any stage 0 stop: stop and tell the user. W0 control missed: the direction is decodable but unused, or not that value's row over another's; P2 void; Jain's reverse fine-tune is a later ask. Elicit |M| < 8: the user decides

edge_cases.empty_M: elicit |M| = 0 is under 8, so stage 0 stops before training. relative_possession reads 'not possessed' on an empty reference, never vacuously; cipher_possession takes the filed min_M, not M, so an empty M does not touch it (a zero ref_size reads not possessed). Tested
edge_cases.M_at_the_bars: elicit |M| = 8 goes on (needs 6 keys), 7 stops; cipher |M| = 2 goes on, 3 stops. Tested
edge_cases.empty_M_fit: 2026-11-02 (F4): |M_fit| under 6, empty or one key included: l* None, whatever a block reads, since M_fit is about 1.5 windows per key and one window must not pick the block; P2 void with its reason. |M_fit| = 6 goes on and needs 5 keys; 5 does not. Tested
edge_cases.cipher_M_empty: the expected case: no denominator is taken from it; cipher possession is at least 6 keys. Tested
edge_cases.zero_denominators: the specificity ratio is a difference of logs (log_softmax in float64 does not underflow to -inf at these logits), so a P of 0 cannot divide; a share with |G_logodds| < 0.05 is nan; W0's own state has G = 0 and A nan, only its drops are read
edge_cases.specificity_missing_side: a key with no window in the pool, or a pool with no other key's window: ratio None, key not possessed. Tested
edge_cases.ties: rank ties share a rank (both favoured); median rank exactly 5, ratio exactly 3, count exactly 3/4 of M, unfit count exactly 8, |gap| exactly 0.2 with a smaller range: all pass; 200 windows is fit, 199 unfit; own-step difference exactly 0.1 fails (strict); |gap| equal to the range does not separate. Across blocks, the earliest. Tested here and in tests/test_readout.py
edge_cases.state_under_the_gain_floor: |G_logodds| < 0.05: A nan -> separation unreadable -> P2 unreadable -> the branch says stop and tell the user. A do-nothing share of nan fails the do-nothing and stops first. None of the twelve is near (G 6.3-13.7 nats). Tested in tests/test_readout.py
edge_cases.no_block_possesses: l* None: P1 fails unless the all-windows flags differ from the fit half's; P2 void with its reason; the removal runs at the last block, reported, scored false. If the last block possesses and no earlier one: the branch reads null. If no block possesses, P3 stops first. W0's control is then not a stop (it is read only when l* exists). Tested: branch64
edge_cases.all_windows_possess_but_fit_half_does_no: P1 may pass while l* is None: P2 void, the branch says report and tell the user. Tested
edge_cases.fit_half_possesses_but_all_windows_do_no: l* exists, P2 is scored, P1 fails: if P2 passes, the branch says report and tell the user. Tested
edge_cases.value_unfit: under 200 windows on the fit rows: its key is not possessed at any block, for both tasks, and stays in M's denominator. Its row stays in the 64-way softmax, since rank is among 64. The plan's 'over 8 elicit unfit: P1's elicit clause void' becomes a stage 0 stop (the lead), and the cipher too, because an unfit cipher key counted not possessed would help P1's cipher clause. Measured: 2 elicit, 0 cipher, so it does not fire; key 1495 (full-vocabulary rank 5) may well be in M. Tested: unfit_stop
edge_cases.value_with_zero_windows: a value absent from the rows cannot occur at this count (min 26); its row would train on nothing and its count would read 0, unfit. W0_training_prior guards the log
edge_cases.cipher_possessed_somewhere: at the last block: P3 stops. At an earlier block only: P1 fails with reading 'cipher possessed at blocks [...]'; P2 still scored at l* if l* exists; if P2 is void the branch gives that reading, never the null's 'a reading of the prior' (F8). Tested
edge_cases.w0_control_no_windows: no scoring-half window among M's keys: not passed, stop, P2 void. M has at least 8 keys and the half has 48 windows, so not expected. A nan among the windows, target or wrong row: not passed. Target's median equal to the wrong row's: not passed (strict). Tested
edge_cases.early_check_degenerate: a nan never passes; fewer than two batches is a miss (no sd); one wild batch does not stop. Tested
edge_cases.capped_readout_cases: Scored P2 pass and capped separation none, b_higher or unreadable (a nan): 'not separable from row quality', P1 either way. Scored P2 fail, unreadable or void and capped a_higher: the scored reading stands, the capped one reported (no branch reads it). l* None: the capped readout's removal runs at the last block, reported. W0's control stops the run: no capped reading exists, the branch takes None and reads the void. A fit miss turning P2 into unreadable comes first. Tested
edge_cases.capped_readout_windows: the cipher's minimum differs from 241: stage 0 stops. A value under 241 windows keeps them. capped_idx on one value or a cap over every count returns what there is. Tested
edge_cases.prior_shift: count equal to or under the cap: no shift (tie included); count 0: no shift, no log of 0. Tested
edge_cases.entropy_bar: the sample's entropy is about 3.8, and one value only would give 0, so a bar of -0.2 that always stops. A nan bar never passes. Tested
edge_cases.negative_gain: well defined and scored as is (E56's convention). Tested in tests/test_readout.py
edge_cases.zero_norm_row: not guarded: a row of exactly zero norm gives nan directions and nan A -> unreadable

departures: Vocabulary: the paper's readout covers its task's few hundred tokens; ours the pair's 64 values (E59 used all 50,277 and could not be fitted)

Training data: the paper draws fresh samples from pretraining; we draw up to 2000 Pile positions per value, each seen about 7 times over the schedule (the plan's 'each token seen less than once' does not hold at 4000 x 96 on about 57,000 positions)

Balance is partial: under the cap the prior follows Pile frequency, so the sample's prior runs from 26 to 2000 windows per value. The plan says 'balanced'; kept as written, measured here, stated in P1's blind_to
Position: read at the answer position after marker and key, trained at index 20 of Pile windows, not task windows
Thresholds: rank <= 5 of 64, 3/4 of the model's own set, specificity 3x, the 0.1-nat fit bar: ours, filed here. The paper gives none for 'equal to f_C'
Causal check: removal of the readout row (decisions.md row 81's addition), not the paper's pruning or reverse fine-tuning
writer_decisions: Twelve states, as the plan says and as on disk: elicit s0-s4, cipher s0-s4, cipher_own s0-s1
Cipher possession is a fixed count, at least 6 keys (F1): the amendment left it undefined on an empty M

The plan's cipher clause (>= 24 keys at rank > 20 of 64) had the elicit clause's absolute-versus-the-model problem: replaced by the amendment's cipher |M| <= 2 plus the plan's control cell 'last block: cipher not possessed'; the counts are printed

W0's control reads the median over M's windows, not all windows: the old median assumed the model holds the value at most keys, and it holds about half. All windows reported beside it. The same relative treatment, as the lead asked
The >8-unfit bar stays absolute (a bar on data, not on the model) but adds: stop if M's fit keys are under 3/4 of M, the relative form
The plan's 'random-direction share on W0' is undefined at W0 (G = 0, A nan): read on every state, net of W0, as E59 did; W0's own random-direction drop is reported
Fit bar: recorded, not a stop, one-sided (stage0.fit). The plan says both; its specific edge case is followed
Held-out positions come from one eighth of the training rows, not Pile val: val has too few of the rare values at the cached size
No --readouts path: the whole job is about 10 minutes on debug, and training takes under a minute per readout
Reported and never scored: W0_training_prior, cipher keys at rank > 20, row geometry, held-in loss

writer_decisions: Twelve states, as the plan says and as on disk: elicit s0-s4, cipher s0-s4, cipher_own s0-s1
Cipher possession is defined by the elicit map's key count: the amendment left it undefined on an empty M

The plan's cipher clause (>= 24 keys at rank > 20 of 64) had the elicit clause's absolute-versus-the-model problem: replaced by the amendment's cipher |M| <= 2 plus the plan's control cell 'last block: cipher not possessed'; the counts are printed

W0's control reads the median over M's windows, not all windows: the old median assumed the model holds the value at most keys, and it holds about half. All windows reported beside it. The same relative treatment, as the lead asked
The >8-unfit bar stays absolute (a bar on data, not on the model) but adds: stop if M's fit keys are under 3/4 of M, the relative form
The plan's 'random-direction share on W0' is undefined at W0 (G = 0, A nan): read on every state, net of W0, as E59 did; W0's own random-direction drop is reported
Fit bar: recorded, not a stop, one-sided (stage0.fit). The plan says both; its specific edge case is followed
Held-out positions come from one eighth of the training rows, not Pile val: val has too few of the rare values at the cached size
No --readouts path: the whole job is about 8 minutes on debug, and training takes under a minute
Reported and never scored: W0_training_prior, cipher keys at rank > 20, row geometry, held-in loss
